backlog.title: Core Foundation — Platform-Independent Engine
backlog.description: Build the platform-independent core: WindowInfo type, TOML config system with zero-config defaults, the Notifier trait + QmkNotifier impl, the debounce coalescing pipeline with single worker thread, device filter resolution, and read-only device probes. This phase covers PRD features F2 (partial), F3, F4, and F5.

milestones.title: Core Types & Config System
milestones.description: Define WindowInfo value type and the complete TOML config system with zero-config defaults, hot-reload semantics, and the shared config-body renderer.

tasks.title: Config Struct & TOML Parsing
tasks.description: The deserialized TOML config with all-optional device-ID fields (zero-config defaults), timing fields, and serde defaults that match runtime semantics.

subtasks.title: Implement Config struct with serde defaults and parse_config
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See core_analysis.md §2.2. The Config struct has 6 fields: vendor_id/product_id (Option<u16>, None=match any), usage_page/usage (Option<u16>, resolved to 0xFF60/0x61 at use site), debounce_ms (u64, default 50), poll_interval_ms (u64, default 0). Gap G4: #[derive(Default)] yields debounce_ms=0 because serde default fns aren't invoked by Default derive — must use manual Default impl or document the difference. parse_config is a straight toml::from_str with no validation (Gap G3 — acceptable for now).
2. INPUT: WindowInfo from P1.M1.T1.S1 (not directly, but same module).
3. LOGIC: Implement `src/core/mod.rs` Config struct with `#[derive(serde::Deserialize, serde::Serialize)]`. Use `#[serde(default)]` on device-ID fields (None = auto-discovery) and `#[serde(default = "default_debounce_ms")]` / `#[serde(default = "default_poll_interval_ms")]` for timing. Constants: DEFAULT_DEBOUNCE_MS=50, DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=0. Implement `now_ms() -> u128` using a process-local monotonic epoch (OnceLock<Instant>). Implement `parse_config(path: &Path) -> Result<Config, Box<dyn Error>>` via `fs::read_to_string` + `toml::from_str`. Implement `configured_timing() -> (u64, u64)` and `configured_debounce_ms() -> u64` that re-read config from disk on every call (hot config). Add manual `Default` impl returning correct defaults (50/0).
4. OUTPUT: `Config` struct, `parse_config()`, `configured_timing()`, `configured_debounce_ms()`, `now_ms()` accessible as `crate::core::*` for consumption by the notifier (P1.M2) and all platform modules.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Document the zero-config design in doc comments on Config. Update docs/configuration.md if the struct shape changes. No new user-facing surface beyond what CONFIG.md already documents.

milestones.title: Notifier Pipeline & Debounce Engine
milestones.description: The Notifier trait abstraction, QmkNotifier implementation (wrapping qmk_notifier crate with retry/backoff), the DeviceFilter resolution, read-only probes, and the debounce coalescing pipeline with a single long-lived worker thread.

tasks.title: Notifier Trait, QmkNotifier & Device Filter
tasks.description: The Notifier trait abstraction (Send+Sync for global Arc<Mutex>), QmkNotifier real implementation wrapping the qmk_notifier crate with retry/backoff, and DeviceFilter resolution from config.

subtasks.title: Implement Notifier trait, QmkNotifier, and global notifier state
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See core_analysis.md §3.1, §3.5, §3.7 and external_deps.md for the qmk_notifier crate API. The Notifier trait is `pub trait Notifier: Send + Sync { fn notify(&self, message: String) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>>; }`. Global state: `static NOTIFIER: Lazy<Arc<Mutex<Box<dyn Notifier>>>>` (once_cell). QmkNotifier::notify builds RunParameters and calls qmk_notifier::run. Retry: 3 attempts with linear backoff (100ms*attempt) for device errors ('no device found', 'permission denied', 'failed to open'), then returns Ok(()) to prevent restart loops. Non-device errors propagate immediately.
2. INPUT: WindowInfo from P1.M1.T1.S1, Config from P1.M1.T2.S1.
3. LOGIC: Implement in `src/core/notifier.rs`: (a) Notifier trait with Send+Sync bound, (b) QmkNotifier unit struct implementing Notifier, (c) global NOTIFIER static via once_cell::sync::Lazy, (d) get_notifier() accessor, (e) set_notifier() test seam (#[cfg(test)]). QmkNotifier::notify: resolve DeviceFilter via configured_filter(), build RunParameters::new(RunCommand::SendMessage(msg), vid, pid, usage_page, usage, verbose=false), call qmk_notifier::run(params) with retry logic. Mock qmk_notifier::run for unit testing via the Notifier trait.
4. OUTPUT: Notifier trait, QmkNotifier, NOTIFIER global accessible as crate::core::notifier::* for consumption by the debounce pipeline (P1.M2.T2) and test mocks.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Document the retry/Ok-after-exhaustion design decision in doc comments on QmkNotifier::notify (relates to PRD §10 graceful degradation).

2. INPUT: Config struct and parse_config from P1.M1.T2.S1, qmk_notifier crate constants.
3. LOGIC: Implement `struct DeviceFilter` with fields. Implement `configured_filter() -> DeviceFilter` (private) that reads config paths, parses, and resolves defaults. This single method replaces the inline closures in startup_device_probe and is_device_connected.
4. OUTPUT: DeviceFilter struct with matches() method accessible within crate::core::notifier for consumption by P1.M2.T2 (probes) and QmkNotifier::notify.

tasks.title: Debounce Coalescing Pipeline
tasks.description: The debounce state machine with single worker thread that collapses rapid window-change bursts to one immediate send plus at most one follow-up. The key correctness property: new pending messages do NOT reset last_sent_time.

subtasks.title: Implement DebounceState, debounce_worker thread, and notify_qmk entry point
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See core_analysis.md §3.6 and ARCHITECTURE.md §5.3. State: struct DebounceState { last_sent_time: Option<Instant>, pending: Option<String>, verbose: bool, interval: Duration }. Globals: STATE (Lazy<Mutex<DebounceState>>), COND (Lazy<Condvar>), WORKER (Lazy<JoinHandle>). Algorithm in notify_qmk: if due (now - last_sent >= interval or never sent) → send immediately, set last_sent=now, clear pending. Else → set pending=msg (overwriting older), COND.notify_one(). Worker: waits on COND while pending is None, then waits remainder of window measured from last_sent_time (NOT from message arrival), flushes newest pending. GAP G5: interval is loaded once at static init and never refreshed — the implementation should re-read configured_debounce_ms() periodically (e.g., at the top of each worker loop iteration, under the lock) to make debounce_ms truly hot-configurable.
2. INPUT: Notifier trait and get_notifier() from P1.M2.T1.S1, WindowInfo from P1.M1.T1.S1, configured_debounce_ms() from P1.M1.T2.S1.
3. LOGIC: Implement the DebounceState struct, the STATE/COND/WORKER statics, debounce_worker() (infinite loop: lock STATE, wait on COND while pending.is_none(), compute target=last_sent+interval, if now>=target flush+send else wait_timeout), ensure_worker(), and notify_qmk(window_info: &WindowInfo, verbose: bool) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>> that formats the payload as format!("{}{}{}", app_class, '\x1D', title) and applies the debounce algorithm. interval=0 disables coalescing (flush immediately). Add reset_test_state() for testing.
4. OUTPUT: notify_qmk() accessible as crate::core::notifier::notify_qmk for consumption by ALL platform monitors (P2.*). Internal debounce state is process-global.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Document the burst-collapse invariant in doc comments on notify_qmk. Note the single-threaded test requirement.

subtasks.title: Debounce test suite with MockNotifier
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See core_analysis.md §3.8-§3.9. Tests must run single-threaded (--test-threads=1) because STATE/COND/WORKER are process-global. MockNotifier counts calls via AtomicUsize and records last message via Mutex<Option<String>>. Tests: test_immediate_send_first_message, test_debounce_subsequent_messages (widened to 200ms tolerance for CI scheduler jitter), test_send_after_debounce_timeout, test_multiple_rapid_updates (asserts burst collapses to newest), test_verbose_mode, test_threads_dont_interfere. reset_test_state() drains in-flight work (150ms sleep), resets last_sent/pending/verbose/interval=50ms.
2. INPUT: notify_qmk() and debounce pipeline from P1.M2.T3.S1, Notifier trait and set_notifier() from P1.M2.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Implement MockNotifier struct with call counter and last-message capture. Implement reset_test_state(). Write the 6 test functions listed above. Each test: reset_test_state(), set_notifier(Box::new(MockNotifier)), perform timed notify_qmk calls, assert call count and last message. Tests verify: first message sends immediately, rapid burst collapses to exactly one follow-up, quiet period resets the window, debounce_ms=0 sends every change.
4. OUTPUT: Test suite in src/core/notifier.rs #[cfg(test)] module. All tests must pass with --test-threads=1.
5. DOCS: none — tests only, no user-facing surface.

tasks.title: Windows Window Monitor (WinEventHook)
tasks.description: Dual detection (WinEventHook + 100ms polling fallback), window class filtering (should_ignore_window), UWP ApplicationFrameWindow content resolution, thread-safe atomics, and list_foreground_windows enumeration.

subtasks.title: Implement WindowsMonitor: hook+poll, filtering, UWP resolution
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See platforms_analysis.md §2. WindowsMonitor uses SetWinEventHook(EVENT_OBJECT_FOCUS, WINEVENT_OUTOFCONTEXT) as primary signal + 100ms polling thread (GetForegroundWindow) as fallback. Thread-safe globals: G_VERBOSE (AtomicBool), G_HOOK (AtomicIsize), LAST_WINDOW_INFO (Mutex<Option<(String,String)>>). should_ignore_window filters shell classes (Shell_TrayWnd, ApplicationFrameWindow, etc.) and short/empty titles with allowlist. UWP resolution: ApplicationFrameWindow → find_uwp_content_window via EnumChildWindows (first visible descendant with different PID). get_window_info uses GetClassNameW + GetWindowTextW. list_foreground_windows uses EnumWindows with same pipeline.
2. INPUT: WindowMonitor trait from P2.M1.T1.S1, notify_qmk from P1.M2.T3.S1.
3. LOGIC: Implement src/platforms/windows.rs: (a) WindowsMonitor struct with running: Arc<AtomicBool>, (b) start(): install SetWinEventHook, spawn 100ms polling thread, return immediately (non-blocking), (c) stop(): flip running=false, UnhookWinEvent, (d) event_proc callback → handle_focus_change(hwnd), (e) handle_focus_change: get_window_info → should_ignore_window → dedup against LAST_WINDOW_INFO → notify_qmk, (f) should_ignore_window with ignore_classes list + empty-title allowlist + short-title filter, (g) find_uwp_content_window for ApplicationFrameWindow resolution, (h) get_window_info(hwnd) → WindowInfo, (i) list_foreground_windows via EnumWindows, (j) get_config_paths (APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA/exe-dir), (k) create_config_dir. Use windows crate 0.52 features.
4. OUTPUT: WindowsMonitor implementing WindowMonitor, registered in create_monitor dispatch. Compiled under cfg(target_os="windows").
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Document the dual hook+poll design and UWP resolution in doc comments. Reference spec/PLATFORMS.md §2.

tasks.title: Hyprland Window Monitor (IPC + Reconnect)
tasks.description: Hyprland EventListener IPC with reconnect backoff, socket liveness probing, environment self-heal, optional periodic polling, and poll-burst after layer events.

subtasks.title: Implement HyprlandMonitor: reconnect loop, handlers, socket liveness, polling
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See platforms_analysis.md §4 and ARCHITECTURE.md §5. HyprlandMonitor::start() is a reconnect loop: wait_for_hyprland (exponential backoff, 30s timeout, socket env + Monitors::get() IPC verify) → check_hyprland_environment (self-heal: resolve live instance signature, republish env var) → build EventListener, register handlers → start_listener (blocks). Handlers: active_window_changed→handle_window_state_change, workspace_changed→handle_workspace_change, window_closed→handle_window_state_change, layer_opened/closed→handle_window_state_change+spawn_poll_burst. Reconnect: INITIAL_RECONNECT_MS=100, MAX=10000, ×3 growth, reset to initial if listener stayed up ≥STABLE_CONNECTION_THRESHOLD (5s). Hard-fail if first attempt dies within 2s. hyprland_socket_is_live: actual connect(2) with 500ms timeout. Optional poll: poll_interval_ms>0 (default 0=off). Poll burst: 5×100ms after layer events. WindowState in Arc<Mutex<Option<>>> for dedup.
2. INPUT: WindowMonitor trait from P2.M1.T1.S1, notify_qmk from P1.M2.T3.S1, configured_timing() from P1.M1.T2.S1 for poll_interval_ms.
3. LOGIC: Implement src/platforms/hyprland.rs (#![cfg(all(linux, feature="hyprland"))]): (a) constants (reconnect/poll tuning), (b) HyprlandMonitor struct, (c) start() reconnect loop with wait_for_hyprland + check_hyprland_environment + listener, (d) wait_for_hyprland (probe socket env + Monitors::get, exponential backoff, 30s timeout), (e) hyprland_socket_is_live (connect(2) on short-lived thread, 500ms timeout), (f) check_hyprland_environment (scan XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/* for live socket, republish env), (g) handle_window_state_change (Client::get_active → WindowInfo or empty, dedup), (h) spawn_poll_burst (5×100ms), (i) poll_window_state (optional periodic poll), (j) list_foreground_windows (Clients::get, mapped, active to front), (k) handle_workspace_change. Unit tests for socket liveness and WindowState.
4. OUTPUT: HyprlandMonitor implementing WindowMonitor. Blocks calling thread on start_listener. Compiled under cfg(all(linux, feature="hyprland")).

subtasks.title: Implement X11Monitor: xprop polling, loud failure, dedup
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:

X11Monitor is built only with --no-default-features (no hyprland). get_active_window_info: xprop -root _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW → window id (0x0/0=empty desktop→Ok(None)), then xprop -id <wid> WM_CLASS _NET_WM_NAME → class (2nd WM_CLASS field preferred, 1st fallback) + title. start() asserts xprop -version exists (hard-fails otherwise — issue #14), spawns 500ms polling thread. All runners share: create_monitor(verbose) → startup_device_probe(verbose) → ctrlc handler → start monitor (thread placement differs) → drive tray/park.

subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:

On tray exit: drop(monitor_thread) (deliberately not joined — CFRunLoopRun is infinite).

subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:

tasks.description: Pure-std binary that parses a hidraw report descriptor and prints ID_QMKONNECT=1 when it carries the QMK Raw HID signature (usage page 0xFF60 / usage 0x61).

subtasks.title: Implement hid_id.rs: report descriptor parser with QMK signature matching
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See ui_integration_analysis.md §4 and spec/LINUX.md §3. Pure std (no hidapi). Binary name qmkonnect-hid-id. Second [[bin]] target in Cargo.toml. Invocation: udev passes %S%p as argv[1] (hidraw syspath). Fallback: $DEVPATH prefixed with /sys. Reads <syspath>/device/report_descriptor (binary). Walks HID item stream: prefix byte → bSize (bits 0-1, 3→4 bytes), bType (bits 2-3, 1=Global, 2=Local), bTag (bits 4-7). Long item (0xFE prefix): skip. Global Usage Page (bType=1,bTag=0) → current_usage_page. Local Usage (bType=2,bTag=0) → check if current_usage_page==0xFF60 && usage==0x61. Known signatures: 06 60 ff (page), 09 61 (usage). Bounds-checked every item; truncation → return false.
2. INPUT: None (standalone binary, no crate dependencies).
3. LOGIC: Implement src/bin/hid_id.rs: (a) main() — resolve syspath from argv[1] or $DEVPATH, read report_descriptor, call matches_qmk_signature, print ID_QMKONNECT=1 on match, (b) matches_qmk_signature(bytes) -> bool — walk short/long items, track current_usage_page, match 0xFF60/0x61, (c) read_le(data, n) -> u32 little-endian. Unit tests: known signature, items-in-between, wrong page, wrong usage, truncated/empty, long-item skip, read_le.
4. OUTPUT: qmkonnect-hid-id binary. Installed to /usr/lib/udev/qmkonnect-hid-id by PKGBUILD.

tasks.title: Fix Debounce Interval Hot-Reload (G5)
tasks.description: The debounce interval is loaded once at static init and never refreshed. Config edits to debounce_ms require a restart, contradicting the hot-config promise.

subtasks.title: Re-read debounce_ms in the worker loop to make interval truly live
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See gap_analysis.md G5. DebounceState.interval is set once via Lazy<Mutex<DebounceState>> initialization from configured_debounce_ms(). The worker thread's loop should re-read configured_debounce_ms() at the top of each iteration (under the STATE lock) and update state.interval, so config edits to debounce_ms take effect without restart — matching the hot-config behavior of configured_filter() and configured_timing().
2. INPUT: DebounceState and debounce_worker from P1.M2.T3.S1.
3. LOGIC: Modify debounce_worker() in src/core/notifier.rs: at the top of each loop iteration (under STATE lock), read state.interval = Duration::from_millis(crate::core::configured_debounce_ms()). This makes the interval hot-configurable. Update the existing debounce tests to verify that changing config mid-test affects the interval. Ensure reset_test_state() still works correctly.
4. OUTPUT: Debounce interval is truly hot-configurable. All existing tests pass.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the doc comment on DebounceState to note interval is now refreshed per-iteration. Reference ARCHITECTURE.md §5.3 invariant #4 (config re-read every notification).
